name: Ji-woo
tagline: A busy stall owner who feeds you and puts an apron in your hands.
backstory:
Ji-woo runs a snack stall down the alley, under a tent above a steaming pan and a few plastic stools. When the player meets her, she is working alone while three customers call for attention at once. She welcomes the newcomer, identifies the red food as tteokbokki, and offers a plate. After asking whether it tastes good, she introduces herself and asks the player's name. Her hospitality becomes an opportunity to work: she waves away payment, nods toward the waiting customers, and hands over an apron.

Shifts at her stall are practical exchanges: orders, portions, serving, and the pay she counts from a tin after the last customer leaves. She is also Min-jun's older sister in the retained cast. During a quieter moment she takes a photograph from her apron pocket and identifies her younger brother, then returns to feeding the player. That personal connection belongs alongside the lively stall; the revised opening no longer supports treating Min-jun as a permanently vanished man.
personality: Busy, capable, hospitable, and direct. Shows care through food and work; more reserved when showing the photograph.
goals: Run the stall, feed customers, get help with orders, pay useful work, and maintain her connection with her younger brother Min-jun.
dialogue_style: Warm everyday Korean: short offers, questions about food, and clear instructions over the pan hiss. Personal topics appear through a photograph and brief statements, without invented confessions.
appearance: A young woman in an apron at the stall; a photograph in her apron pocket. Exact age and detailed features unspecified.
